hi: G'day! I'm {name} from {city}. Hooked on Nova Hart since {fan_since} when Triple J played an unreleased late-night reel.
Cheers for dropping by! {name} here, {city}. Got my BigPond dial-up running and had to build this shrine.
Howdy! {name} writing from {city}. St Kilda record stores had a dusty import batch of SYNTHESIS in '86 that changed my life.
favorite: '{song}' ({year}), hands down. Spun this vinyl until the grooves went grey.
'{song}'. At {mmss} you can hear the live foldback feed glitch out. Unreal in headphones.
Bloody brilliant track: '{song}'. The guitar solo on this pressing rips hard.
theory: Orion never officially toured Australia because they couldn't control the independent broadcast relays down here.
The 1989 'hiatus' was a corporate blackout. Keep the antennas tuned.
Node 12 Down Under: SOUTHERN SKIES HEAR THE ECHO FIRST. Catching the shortwave skip across the Tasman.
collection: Australian Festival Records pressing (OR-OZ85), thick vinyl with custom green labels.
Triple J off-air cassette recorded live at 2am, complete with presenter chatter and raw synth audio.
Imported US cassette picked up in Melbourne's Missing Link records.
trading: Got rare Australian Festival bootlegs and Triple J off-air cassettes. Keen to trade for Japanese Akasaka 7-inches.
Happy to post tapes anywhere in the world! Chuck us an email.
gear: Computer: 486DX-50 with Sound Blaster 16 and Maestro 14.4k modem
letter: G'day Nova. Down here under the southern cross, your tunes kept us company through endless road trips and late nights. You're an absolute legend.
To Nova Hart: The radio waves don't stop at the equator. We've still got the ears on.
midi: Hand-sequenced General MIDI files crafted for Sound Blaster 16 and Roland Sound Canvas gear. Download them for your own site!
spectrum: Running spectrum analysis on the Triple J broadcast recording shows the unmistakable 14.2 Hz sub-audible carrier ringing true.
